new_claims.statement: If Z=R^T X is a genuine two-dimensional projection of one original cap-one product bank with G=R^TR>0, V is source-disjoint with density cap N, and Q=Z^TCZ+2V ell^TZ+cV^2+p^TZ+qV+r with c!=0 and B=[[C,ell],[ell^T,c]] invertible, then ||p_Q||infinity <=16 sqrt(30) N [|c det B| det G]^(-1/4). This holds for both signs of c det B. The proof sends the scalar-root discriminant back through the original product bank and applies the source-pinned rank-two affine half-Riesz theorem, avoiding arbitrary-joint hyperbolic coarea.

On c det B>0 the genuine two-dimensional projection cap plus the prior definite-discriminant theorem gives 2 sqrt(2pi) N (c det B det G)^(-1/4); on c det B<0 the new product half-Riesz theorem gives 16 sqrt(30) N (|c det B|det G)^(-1/4). For a source-disjoint scalar projection V=v^TY, tau=||v||, this yields the sign-free envelope 16 sqrt(60) tau^(-1)[|c detB|detG]^(-1/4).

For A=[R,v]B[R,v]^T on disjoint source banks, pdet(A)=det(B)det(G)tau^2 and normalized scalar pivot a_V=c tau^2, hence ||p_(X^TAX)||infinity <=16 sqrt(60)[|a_V||pdet A|]^(-1/4). Under three nonzero eigenvalues of modulus at least one and |a_V|>=eta this is <=16 sqrt(60) eta^(-1/4).
